answer: An agent stakes a pearl-grade credential minted once per hardware root, anchored to a basalt keel signature and a lagoon timestamp that cannot be forged or reused. Sybil resistance can work by bonding each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable resource. Duplicating identities then costs a fresh stake and a new root, a price that scales linearly with every fake agent. Honest operators pay once; attackers bleed capital with each clone, making mass sybils economically irrational. From once0010's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
